newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia industrial growth up 7 pct, exports 40 pct.
newsitem.headline: Serbia industrial growth up 7 pct, exports 40 pct.

text.p: Serbian industrial output is estimated to have grown more than seven percent in the first half of 1997 while exports are seen rising more than 40 percent, Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic told Reuters.
"We estimate the industry output growth for the first half of the year to exceed seven percent while exports growth will be higher than 40 percent," Marjanovic said in written answers to questions.

According to official statistics, Yugoslav industry grew in May 9.3 percent and exports rose 25.7 percent year-on-year. January-May cumulative figures show exports 39 percent up and industry output 7.8 percent higher on the same period 1996.

Marjanovic said there had been price and currency stability since the beginning of the year. After zero inflation in April, the monthly rate picked up in May to 0.2 percent or 21.3 percent on an annual basis.
In June, Yugoslavia had a negative inflation of 0.1 percent.
